\eta_\pm(y\mid x)=1\pm\varepsilon g(x)h(y).
\]
These are normalized, strictly positive \(C^\infty\) conditional densities satisfying the required sectional Hölder and density bounds after choosing \(\varepsilon\) small enough; they may be embedded in the causal model with \(e\equiv1/2\) and a uniform control arm. Since \(\int_{[0,1]^d}g(x)\,dx=0\), both marginal mixtures equal the uniform law, so \(W_1(Q_{1,+},Q_{1,-})=0\). At each \(x\),
\[
W_1\!\left(\eta_+(\cdot\mid x),\eta_-(\cdot\mid x)\right)
=\frac{2\varepsilon|g(x)|}{\pi^2},
\]
because the laws differ only in their first outcome coordinate. Hence their design-averaged conditional distance is \(4\varepsilon/\pi^3>0\). Thus GANICE’s extended \(W_1\) distinguishes conditional rearrangements that the marginal-mixture \(W_1\) intentionally identifies, and its extended-loss minimax lower bound cannot supply a lower bound—or an exact frontier—for the proposed marginal loss.”

Hidden issue to preserve explicitly: do not say GANICE has “no implication” for marginal \(W_1\). Convexity gives
\[
W_1\!\left(\int\mu_x\,dx,\int\nu_x\,dx\right)
\le \int W_1(\mu_x,\nu_x)\,dx,
\]
so a compatible extended-\(W_1\) upper bound can imply a possibly nonsharp marginal upper bound. The witness establishes strict nonequivalence and blocks transfer of the extended-loss lower bound and exact minimax frontier, not every possible upper-bound implication.
